content.overview: BNS s. 159 — Abetting mutiny, or attempting to seduce a soldier, sailor or airman from his duty.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Abetting mutiny, or attempting to seduce a soldier, sailor or airman from his duty. BNS restatement of IPC 131. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 131. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 159 is the rule on “Abetting mutiny, or attempting to seduce a soldier, sailor or airman from his duty”. The section provides that whoever abets the committing of mutiny by an officer, soldier, sailor or airman, in the Army, Navy or Air Force of the Government of India or attempts to seduce any such officer, soldier, sailor or airman from his allegiance or his duty, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 159 exists so that “Abetting mutiny, or attempting to seduce a soldier, sailor or airman from his duty” has a closed legal test in Chapter VIII — Of Offences Relating to the Army, Navy and Air Force. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Mutiny, desertion, insubordination, and wearing a service garb.

The provision in detail
